learningObjectives.title: Compound shapes and parts of shapes

questions.q: How many square centimetres (cm²) are there in 1 square metre (m²)?
questions.explain: Since 1 m = 100 cm, an area is scaled by 100² = 10 000, so 1 m² = 10 000 cm².

questions.q: How many cubic centimetres (cm³) are equal to 1 litre?
questions.explain: One litre is defined as 1 000 cm³ (equivalently 1 000 millilitres).

questions.q: What is the formula for the area of a triangle with base b and perpendicular height h?
questions.explain: The area of a triangle is half the base multiplied by the perpendicular height.

questions.q: A trapezium has parallel sides a and b and perpendicular height h. Which formula gives its area?
questions.explain: The area of a trapezium is the average of the two parallel sides multiplied by the height.

questions.q: Which expression gives the circumference of a circle of diameter d?
questions.explain: The circumference equals π times the diameter, equivalently 2πr.

questions.q: What is the formula for the area of a circle of radius r?
questions.explain: The area of a circle is π multiplied by the radius squared.

questions.q: What is the volume of a cylinder of radius r and height h?
questions.explain: The volume of a cylinder is the circular cross-sectional area πr² multiplied by the height.

questions.q: Which formula gives the volume of a sphere of radius r?
questions.explain: The volume of a sphere is four-thirds of π multiplied by the radius cubed.

questions.q: A cube has sides of length 1 metre. What is its volume expressed in cubic centimetres (cm³)?
questions.explain: Volume is scaled by 100³ = 1 000 000, so 1 m³ = 1 000 000 cm³.

questions.q: Why is the area of a parallelogram found using base × perpendicular height rather than base × slant side?
options: Because the slant side is always longer than the base
Because the perpendicular height gives the true vertical distance between the parallel sides
Because parallelograms have no perpendicular height
Because the slant side equals the diagonal
questions.explain: Area depends on the perpendicular distance between the parallel sides, not the sloping length of the side.

questions.q: For a sector with angle θ° at the centre of a circle of radius r, which expression gives the arc length?
questions.explain: The arc is the fraction θ/360 of the full circumference 2πr.

questions.q: Which expression gives the area of a sector with centre angle θ° in a circle of radius r?
questions.explain: The sector area is the fraction θ/360 of the whole circle area πr².

questions.q: Which expression gives the curved (lateral) surface area of a cylinder of radius r and height h?
questions.explain: Unrolling the curved surface gives a rectangle of width 2πr (the circumference) and height h.

questions.q: A cone and a cylinder have the same base radius and the same height. How does the cone's volume compare?
options: The cone has the same volume
The cone has half the volume
The cone has one third of the volume
The cone has twice the volume
questions.explain: Volume of a cone is ⅓πr²h, exactly one third of a cylinder πr²h with equal radius and height.

questions.q: Which formula gives the surface area of a sphere of radius r?
questions.explain: The surface area of a sphere is 4π multiplied by the radius squared.

questions.q: What is the most reliable method for finding the area of a compound shape?
options: Multiply all the given side lengths together
Split it into simpler shapes, find each area, then add or subtract as needed
Always use the formula for a circle
Measure only the longest side and square it
questions.explain: Compound shapes are broken into standard shapes whose areas are then combined by addition or subtraction.
